title: Create a suppliers table
prompt: Create a table named suppliers with three columns. id is an integer and the primary key. name is text and must always have a value. active is a boolean that must always have a value and is true when an INSERT leaves it out. The starter has the columns but none of the rules.
hints: Three rules are missing: one identifies a row, one forbids a missing name, one supplies a value.
Rules are written after the column's type.
id integer PRIMARY KEY, name text NOT NULL, active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true
verify: INSERT INTO suppliers (id, name) VALUES (1, 'Acme') RETURNING id, name, active;
rejects: INSERT INTO suppliers (id, name) VALUES (2, NULL)
INSERT INTO suppliers (id, name, active) VALUES (3, 'Bolt', NULL)

wrongAnswers.misconception: Leaves out the primary key, so two suppliers can share an id.
Gives active no default, so a missing value is stored as NULL.

feedback: Read which statement the check ran. Either a row came back with the wrong value, or a bad row was accepted.
